About
Minimal Gallery is a curated source of website design inspiration aiming to support people in their creative process. Running since 2013.
The site was originally brought to life as a passion project by
Piet Therheyden
(acquired in 2026).
Seeing the need for a website gallery to help designers with inspiration for client projects, he started building the first version back in early 2013.
Minimal Gallery has since become one of the leading web design galleries, followed by tens of thousands of designers, developers, agencies, marketing specialists and entrepreneurs all over the world.
If you have created or know a beautiful website, template or a useful tool, you're welcome to
Submit

By submitting content, you represent and warrant that:
The URL you submit is publicly accessible and you have a good-faith belief that it is appropriate for inclusion in a design inspiration gallery.

We do not claim ownership of the submitted websites/tools themselves. However, the screenshots, thumbnails, curated descriptions, metadata, and overall presentation on minimal.gallery are our original work and property.

All content on minimal.gallery — including screenshots, thumbnails, layout, design, text, graphics, and metadata — is owned by us or our licensors and protected by copyright, trademark, and other intellectual property laws.
You may not reproduce, distribute, modify, display, or use any images (screenshots/thumbnails), designs, or other Site content for commercial or public purposes without our prior written permission. This includes scraping, downloading images in bulk, or republishing the gallery on other platforms.

4. Affiliate Links
Some links on this Site may be affiliate links. This means that if you click on certain links and make a purchase, we may earn a small commission at no additional cost to you. These commissions help support the maintenance and growth of minimal.gallery. We only recommend resources we believe are valuable to our visitors.
5. Privacy Policy

Submission Form
: Personal information such as your name and email address, the submitted URL, and any other voluntary information you provide.
Newsletter

Usage Data / Analytics

Plausible Analytics
, a privacy-friendly and GDPR-compliant service, to collect standard, anonymized usage data such as pages visited, device type, referrer, and general traffic trends. Plausible does not use cookies and does not collect any personal data.
Local Storage & Cookies
: We may use browser local storage and/or cookies to support features such as saving your bookmarked websites. These are stored on your device and are not transmitted to our servers.
5.2 How We Use Your Information
Process and review your submissions.

Comply with legal obligations.

not

).

We retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes described or as required by law. You may request deletion of your personal data by contacting us.

Listing Guidelines
Version
1.1
· Effective
18 September 2026
These guidelines describe what can be listed in the DesignBookmark directory. They apply to every listing, whether we added it ourselves or you submitted it. Submitting is free, every submission is read by a person before it is published, and by submitting a tool you confirm that it meets these guidelines.
What qualifies
A listing is a single tool, website, app or resource that a designer, developer or person working with AI would find useful. It has to be something a visitor can actually go and use.
It must be a real, working product or service, live at the URL you submit.
It must be relevant to one of our published categories: design, development, AI, no-code and web, marketing and growth, productivity, business, content and media, platforms, libraries and templates, or learning and community.
It must fit an existing category. We do not create new categories for individual submissions.
It must be understandable in English, since that is the language of the directory.
Quality requirements
The URL must be a secure address, starting with
https://
, and must load without a login wall, an interstitial or a country block.
The name is what people call the product. Not a slogan, not a keyword string.
The description is one plain sentence saying what the tool does, up to 200 characters. Not marketing copy, not a list of keywords.
The site must be substantially complete. A waiting list page, a coming-soon holding page, or a page that is still placeholder content does not qualify.
What we will not list
Scams, fraudulent offers, or anything designed to deceive people about what it is or who runs it.
Malware, phishing, or anything that puts a visitor's device or accounts at risk.
Content that is illegal where we operate, or that infringes someone else's copyright or trademark.
Adult or sexually explicit material.
Parked domains, expired domains and domains for sale.
Pages that exist mainly to carry affiliate links, redirect elsewhere or funnel traffic rather than provide the tool itself.
Submissions that misrepresent the product, its ownership, its price or its capabilities.
Link shorteners, tracking redirects and URLs that do not resolve directly to the product.
Duplicates
Each product gets one listing. We check submissions against the directory by name and by domain, and a tool that is already listed cannot be listed a second time. If your product is already in the directory and something about the entry is wrong, email us and we will correct it.
Separate products from the same company can each be listed, provided each one meets these guidelines on its own. Two URLs that lead to substantially the same product are a duplicate, not two products.
How your submission is published
A person reads every submission against these guidelines before anything is published, so listing is not automatic and there is no fixed turnaround. If we do list it, the name, URL, category and description you entered are what get published. Nobody rewrites them for you. We may make small edits for consistency: fixing capitalisation, trimming a description to fit, correcting obvious typos, standardising how a name is written, or moving an entry to a category that fits it better. We will not change what your product is or what it claims to do.
We also capture a screenshot of the submitted page and store a copy of the site's icon, so the listing has an image. Both are refreshed from time to time.
Removal
We may remove a listing that no longer meets these guidelines. In practice that means one of the following: the site has gone offline or become a parked domain; the product has materially changed into something that would not have qualified; the submission misrepresented the product; or the listing turns out to fall into the "what we will not list" section above.
Removal is covered by our
Terms & Conditions
. We will always tell you at the email address on the submission.
If you disagree
Email
hello@designbookmark.com
and a person will look at it. If we got it wrong, we will put the listing back.

Privacy Policy
Last updated 3 October 2026
This policy explains what DesignBookmark collects, what we do with it, and who else is involved. DesignBookmark ("we", "us") is the directory published at designbookmark.com, and is responsible for the personal data described here. Contact us at
hello@designbookmark.com
.
What we collect
If you just browse:
analytics data about the pages you visit, described below. No account is needed and we do not ask for your name.
If you create an account:
your email address and basic profile information from Google sign-in, plus the tools you bookmark.
If you subscribe to the newsletter:
your email address, the date you confirmed, and which page you subscribed from.
If you submit a tool:
the tool's name, URL, category and description, plus your email address. Submitting is free, so there is no payment and no payment record.
Google sign-in and your Google data
Signing in is optional and only needed to save bookmarks. When you choose
Sign in with Google
, we ask Google for the standard
openid, email and profile
permissions and nothing else. From them we receive your email address, your name and your profile picture.
How we use it:
to create your account, keep you signed in, show your name and picture in the account menu, and attach your bookmarks to you so they sync across devices.
The newsletter, only if you ask:
signing in never subscribes you. If you click Subscribe while signed in, we add your account email to the weekly drop, and you can unsubscribe from any issue.
Where it is stored:
in our Supabase database, together with the bookmarks you save.
What we never do:
we do not read your Gmail, contacts, calendar, Drive or any other Google data; we do not sell it, share it with advertisers, use it for advertising, or use it to train AI models.
Deleting it:
email hello@designbookmark.com and we delete your account, your Google profile details and your bookmarks within 30 days. You can also revoke DesignBookmark's access at any time from your Google Account under Security, Third-party apps.
DesignBookmark's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the
Google API Services User Data Policy
, including the Limited Use requirements.
What becomes public, and what does not
When a listing is published, the
name, URL, category and description
become publicly visible on the site and to search engines. We also capture and publish a screenshot of the submitted page and a copy of the site's icon.
Your email address is never published.
Neither are your bookmarks, your account details, or a submission we did not publish. We do not sell personal data, and we do not share it for advertising.
Who processes data for us
Supabase.
Our database and file storage: accounts, bookmarks, submissions, newsletter subscribers, screenshots, icons.
Google.
Sign-in, if you choose to create an account, and Google Analytics 4.
Resend.
Sending email: newsletter issues, listing notifications and confirmation links.
Web3Forms.
A notification to our inbox when a tool is submitted.
Hotjar.
Session replay and heatmaps, so we can see how pages are actually used.
Cloudflare.
Hosting, DNS and caching for the site.
Analytics and tracking, plainly
We use
Google Analytics 4
to understand which pages and tools people find useful. It records page views, searches made on the site, which cards and outbound links are clicked, and coarse location and device information. We never send it your email address, your bookmarks, or the free text of anything you submit.
We use
Hotjar
for session replay and heatmaps. This records how a page is scrolled, moved through and clicked. It is used to find layout problems, not to identify individuals, and Hotjar suppresses text typed into form fields by default.
Both set cookies or similar identifiers in your browser. You can block both with any content blocker, or with your browser's own controls, and the site works normally if you do. We do not run advertising trackers.
Screenshots of listed sites
For every tool in the directory we capture an image of its public homepage and a copy of its icon, and serve them from our own storage rather than hot-linking. This is standard directory practice and applies to every entry alike. If you own a listed site and want its screenshot removed, email us.
How long we keep things
Published listings:
for as long as the listing is in the directory.
Submissions we did not publish:
kept as a record rather than deleted, so we can tell you why if you ask.
Records of past paid listings:
while the listing fee existed, payments were handled by Polar Software, Inc. as merchant of record. We keep those payment references for as long as we need them for accounting and tax, which is usually several years, and Polar keeps its own records independently. No new payments are taken through the site.
Newsletter subscribers:
until you unsubscribe, which you can do from any issue.
Accounts and bookmarks:
until you ask us to delete the account.
Analytics:
according to Google's and Hotjar's own retention settings.
Your choices
You can ask us for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. Email
hello@designbookmark.com
and we will respond within 30 days. You can also ask us to take a published listing down; see the
Terms
.
You can unsubscribe from the newsletter with the link in any issue. You can block analytics as described above.
Links out
DesignBookmark links to third-party tools and websites, and some links may earn us a commission at no cost to you. Once you leave, the privacy policy of the destination site applies, not ours.
Changes
We will date any changes to this policy on this page.

. Nothing is paid through this site. The terms of any sponsorship, including start date, duration and payment, are agreed separately in writing between us and the sponsor.
